name: Gateway Arch
headline: height
subtitle: Gateway Arch National Park, St. Louis, Missouri
description: The Gateway Arch is a stainless-steel monument in St. Louis, designed by architect Eero Saarinen to commemorate Thomas Jefferson's vision. It has the shape of a weighted catenary, and its steel skin carries its own weight without an internal frame. The National Park Service gives it a maximum height of 630 ft (192 m) and the same 630 ft width between the outer faces of its legs, and calls it the nation's tallest monument.

measures.label: Maximum height
measures.note: Maximum height of the arch (192 m)

measures.label: Outer width
measures.note: From the outside of the north leg to the outside of the south leg (192 m)

measures.label: Leg dimension at base
measures.note: Size of each leg's triangular cross-section at the base (16.46 m); it narrows to 17 ft (5.18 m) at the top

measures.label: Total steel weight
measures.note: All steel in the arch, in metric tons; the fact sheet also gives 5,199 tons

measures.label: Total concrete weight
measures.note: All concrete, in metric tons (the fact sheet also gives 38,107 Tons)

facts.text: The foundations are reinforced concrete reaching 60 ft deep, with 30 ft set into bedrock.
The outer skin is 900 tons of polished stainless steel in panels 1/4 in thick, over an inner wall of 3/8 in carbon steel.
The arch is built from 142 sections and is designed to deflect 18 in in a 150 mph wind.
The Park Service's construction sequence shows the arch rising between February 29, 1964 and October 28, 1965.

caveats: The fact sheet gives the steel weight as 5,199 tons and 4,644 metric tons, which do not convert exactly into each other; the metric figure is stored.
The steel and concrete weights are listed separately and the foundations are reinforced concrete, so neither figure is the weight of the visible arch alone.
